disabled.title: Finance is not enabled
disabled.desc: The accounting module is switched off for this deployment.

forbidden.title: No access to finance
forbidden.desc: Ask an administrator for the accounting permission.

mode.label: Stripe environment
mode.testBanner: TEST MODE — you are viewing Stripe test data. Nothing here is real money.

reason.CODE_NOT_FOUND: Event code detected — no event with this code yet

agreement.title: Commercial agreement
agreement.help: How Bilit's commission is calculated for this event. Components add up; leave a value at 0 to not use it. Changing it later creates a new version — past sales keep the version they were booked with.
agreement.gross: Percentage of what the customer paid
agreement.net: Percentage of what the customer paid − Stripe fee
agreement.perTicketHint: Ticket count from Stripe metadata (default 1 per payment)
agreement.eventFeeHint: Charged once to the organiser when you post it
agreement.reverse: Refunds reverse the commission pro rata
agreement.added: Added on top of the ticket price (customer pays ticket + fee)

dashboard.title: Finance dashboard
dashboard.sub: Based on imported Stripe transactions and the accounting ledger. Each currency is shown separately — nothing is converted.
dashboard.emptyDesc: Connect Stripe and run a synchronisation to import transactions.
dashboard.asOfEnd: At the end of the period
dashboard.unallocatedHint: Stripe money not yet linked to an event
dashboard.attentionDesc: Some Stripe money is not yet assigned to an event or account.
dashboard.explain: Gross sales is what customers paid. Stripe fees are taken from Stripe's own balance transactions. Organiser payable = gross − refunds − Stripe fees (when the organiser bears them) − Bilit commission. Outstanding = payable − payments made. Payouts move money from Stripe to the bank and are never counted as sales.

tx.title: Stripe transactions
tx.sub: Every Stripe balance transaction, with gross, fee and net kept separately.
tx.search: Search ID, description or event code
tx.emptyDesc: Run a Stripe sync, or change the filters.

detail.title: Stripe transaction
detail.amountsSale: The whole sale: the payment plus every refund and dispute that belongs to it.
detail.ledgerDesc: Double-entry postings for this transaction, including reversals.
detail.unmatchDesc: The ledger posting is reversed and the money moves to unallocated receipts. Automatic matching will not reassign it.
detail.onTop: added on top of ticket price

match.title: Assign to event
match.desc: The ledger is re-posted (the previous posting is reversed, never edited) and the change is recorded in the audit log.
match.reasonHint: Required. Shown in the audit log.
match.overrideConfirm: I confirm this assignment despite the warning

events.title: Events
events.sub: Accounting events with their unique event code, organiser and commission agreement. Stripe payments are matched to events by code.
events.formDesc: The event code must be unique. Stripe payment descriptions or metadata containing it are matched to this event.
events.emptyDesc: Create an event and give it the code used in Stripe payment descriptions.
events.name: Name
events.codeHint: e.g. EVT-BER-2026-001 — letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore
events.organiserHint: Payments are only allocated once an organiser is linked
events.noOrganiserWarn: No organiser linked — payments stay unmatched
events.changeReasonHint: Required when the event already has transactions
events.profitDesc: From the ledger. Revenue, cash, Stripe fees, organiser payable and Bilit profit are separate concepts.
events.agreementsDesc: Every version is kept. Sales record the version used to calculate them.
events.newAgreementDesc: Applies to transactions imported or re-assigned from now on. Already-booked sales are not recalculated.
events.feePosted: Event fee charged to the organiser
events.onTop: added on top of ticket price

organisers.title: Organisers
organisers.sub: Accounting organisers are created here by an administrator — never automatically from Stripe customers.
organisers.formDesc: Bank details are encrypted and only shown after re-authentication.
organisers.search: Search name, company, email or ID
organisers.emptyDesc: Create an organiser, then link it to its events.
organisers.name: Name
organisers.bankHelp: Stored encrypted. Leave empty if unknown.
organisers.eventsDesc: Events belonging to this organiser. Stripe sales for these events count towards the organiser's balance.
organisers.statementDesc: Every booking that changes what Bilit owes this organiser, with a running balance.

pay.title: Payments to this organiser
pay.desc: Every payment made to the organiser, with receipts. Voided payments are kept for the audit trail.

ref.title: Refunds & chargebacks
ref.desc: Refunds on this organiser's events. The booking-fee part is charged to the organiser.

rep.title: Reports
rep.desc: Download reports for this organiser. Choose a period first; all reports use the same period.

account.title: Account report (PDF) — organiser copy
account.desc: Summary, settlement by event, all payments and refunds. Ticket sales shown net of booking fees — ready to send to the organiser.

internal.title: Account report (PDF) — internal
internal.desc: Same report with booking fees and Bilit profit. Not for the organiser.

refunds.title: Refunds statement (PDF)
refunds.desc: Every refund and chargeback with the booking fee to recover.

statement.title: Account statement (CSV)
statement.desc: Running balance of every ledger line, for the selected currency.

payments.title: Payments (CSV)
payments.desc: All payments made to this organiser.

st.title: Settlement statement
st.desc: Choose the events to settle — finished and cancelled events are ticked for you. The PDF lists each event, every payment made and the balance still due. Payments not tied to an event are applied to this statement.
st.none: This organiser has no events yet.

con.title: Contracts
con.desc: Contracts linked to this organiser — master agreement and event schedules. An event should not go live until its contract is signed by both parties.
con.emptyDesc: Link the signed Promoter Master Agreement and each Event Schedule.
con.name: Contract
con.dialogDesc: Search contracts by reference, name or recipient.
con.goLive: Contract active — event can go live
con.notLive: No active contract — do not put this event live

organisers.cashbackHelp: A % of each finished event's ticket sales after refunds (excluding the booking fee) that Bilit gives back to this organiser. It is added to what they are owed and paid with the settlement. Applied when an event is marked Finished.

payments.title: Organiser payments
payments.sub: Money Bilit paid to organisers. Each payment is its own ledger entry and reduces the outstanding balance; Stripe data is never changed.
payments.recordDesc: Records a payment from Bilit's bank account to the organiser.
payments.emptyDesc: Record payments as you make them so outstanding balances stay correct.
payments.eventHint: Optional — leave empty for a payment covering several events
payments.voidDesc: The payment is kept, marked VOIDED, and its ledger entry is reversed.

stripe.title: Stripe
stripe.sub: Connection, webhooks and synchronisation for the selected environment.

conn.title: Stripe integration — {mode}
conn.desc: Server-side API key, encrypted at rest. The key is never shown again or sent to the browser.
conn.keyDesc: Use a restricted key (recommended) with read access only.
conn.perms: Read: Balance, Balance transactions, Charges, PaymentIntents, Refunds, Disputes, Payouts. Optional write: Webhook endpoints (only to register the webhook automatically).
conn.disconnectDesc: The stored key and webhook secret are destroyed. Imported transactions and the ledger are kept.

webhook.title: Webhook
webhook.desc: Stripe notifies Bilit immediately; every event is signature-verified and processed once. A scheduled sync every 30 minutes covers any gap.
webhook.autoDesc: Creates the endpoint {url} in Stripe and stores its signing secret. Needs Webhook Endpoints write access.
webhook.manualDesc: From the Stripe Dashboard endpoint, or printed by `stripe listen` for local testing.

cli.title: Local development with the Stripe CLI
cli.desc: Production never depends on the CLI. For local testing, forward test-mode events to your machine and paste the whsec_ secret it prints into test mode.

log.title: Webhook events
log.desc: Received Stripe events. Payloads are not trusted: each one triggers a fresh fetch from the Stripe API.

security.title: Security
security.desc: Stripe credentials are encrypted (AES-256-GCM) and never exposed to the browser, logs or API responses. Changing them requires re-authentication and is audited.

payouts.title: Payouts
payouts.sub: Transfers from the Stripe balance to Bilit's bank account. A payout is not a sale.
payouts.linkHelp: If a Stripe payout was money paid to an organiser, use “Link to organiser”: it records an organiser payment with the payout's amount, date and payout id as reference — choose the organiser and event code. Payouts that are Bilit's own money need no link.
payouts.selectAll: Select all unlinked payouts on this page
payouts.bulkDesc: Each payout becomes its own organiser payment (amount, arrival date, payout id as reference, method Stripe). Payouts already linked are skipped.
payouts.bulkEventHint: Optional — otherwise they count towards the organiser's account but not a specific event
payouts.bulkConfirm: These payouts were money paid to this organiser

sync.title: Stripe sync
sync.sub: Import Stripe balance transactions and payouts in the background. Safe to run any number of times.
sync.idempotent: Running a sync twice never creates duplicate transactions or ledger entries.
sync.running: A run is in progress — this page refreshes automatically.
sync.errorsDesc: Already-processed transactions are kept; retry re-fetches only these.
sync.how: Stripe balance transactions are the source of truth: each one is imported once (unique Stripe ID), matched to an event by its code and posted to the ledger. A failing transaction is recorded and skipped without stopping the run; large imports resume from where they stopped.

recon.title: Reconciliation
recon.sub: Transactions that need attention, and a check of the ledger against Stripe.
recon.neverRun: Not run yet — it also runs after every sync.
recon.problemsDesc: {ledger} transaction(s) do not match their ledger posting; {charges} successful charge(s) have no balance transaction yet.
recon.stripeDiffNote: The difference to Stripe's balance is only expected to be zero after a full historical sync.
recon.queueDesc: No event code, unknown code, inactive event, no organiser, currency mismatch, duplicates or missing classification.

reports.title: Reports
reports.sub: Sales, event profitability and Stripe reconciliation. CSV exports use plain decimal amounts and open directly in Excel.

d.sales: One row per Stripe payment with its refunds and fees.
d.event-profit: One row per event and currency, from the ledger.
d.reconciliation: Every Stripe transaction with its accounting status.

more.statementDesc: Per organiser and currency, with CSV export.

ledger.title: Accounting ledger
ledger.sub: Double-entry journal. Entries are append-only: corrections are reversals, never edits or deletions.
ledger.reverseDesc: An equal and opposite entry is posted; the original stays in the ledger marked REVERSED.

adj.title: Manual adjustment
adj.desc: Posts a balanced entry in the {mode} mode books. Stripe transactions are never altered.

presets.organiserCharge: Charge organiser: organiser payable → Bilit fees
presets.organiserCredit: Credit organiser: other expenses → organiser payable

periods.title: Accounting periods
periods.desc: A closed month accepts no new postings (enforced by the database). Late Stripe activity is booked in the current open period with its original date kept. Reopening requires a reason and is audited.
periods.none: No closed periods — all months are open.
periods.allClear: Nothing open — this month is ready to close.
periods.ack: I have reviewed the open items and want to close the month anyway

settings.title: Finance settings
settings.sub: How Stripe payments are matched to events, and accounting defaults.
settings.baseHint: For reporting; other currencies are never silently converted
settings.defaultModeHint: Which Stripe mode the finance screens open on
settings.qtyKeyHint: Used for per-ticket commission; default 1 per payment
settings.timezone: Posting dates use the organisation time zone ({tz}).
settings.rulesDesc: Tried in order. The first rule that finds a code which exists in Bilit wins; several different codes are never guessed.
settings.patternHint: First capture group is the code
settings.exactDesc: Matches any existing event code that appears as a word in the payment description.
settings.how: Put the event code in Stripe metadata (event_code) for new payments; keep the description rule for existing payments that only carry it in the description.

link.title: Link events to this organiser
link.desc: Choose the events this organiser runs. Detected codes become new events under this organiser, and their existing Stripe sales are matched straight away.
link.detectedDesc: Taken from payment descriptions (e.g. “for event: Blood In Blood Out Berlin (B41-0091)”). The name is the text before the code — edit it if needed.
link.noneDetected: No unlinked event codes found in Stripe.
link.name: Event name

import.title: Import events from Stripe transactions
import.desc: Event codes found in payment descriptions that have no event yet. The name is the text after “event:” and before the code. Their sales are matched as soon as the event exists and has an organiser.
import.none: No new event codes found in the imported transactions. Run a Stripe sync first.
import.name: Event name
import.organiserNote: Events without an organiser are created, but their sales stay unmatched until you link an organiser (from the event or organiser page).

fin.otherCurrency: Showing {c} activity booked to this {e} event.
fin.paidShare: Share of the amount due already paid

kpi.dueHint: After booking fee, refunds and deductions
kpi.margin: Margin {fees}% of Bilit's fees · {sales}% of sales

flow.title: Where the money went
flow.desc: Customers paid → booking fee → organiser money → paid → remaining.
flow.deductionsHint: Fixed event fees and manual adjustments
flow.feeInRefunds: of which booking fee refunded (charged to organiser)

pl.title: Event profitability
pl.desc: Bilit's profit and loss for {event}, straight from the ledger.
pl.grossHint: Customer money; most of it belongs to the organiser
pl.bilitBorneHint: Where the agreement leaves the loss with Bilit

separation.title: Who the money belongs to
separation.desc: Ticket revenue, booking fee, organiser money and Bilit profit kept apart.

terms.title: Booking fee & commercial terms
terms.desc: Each change creates a new version. The booking fee can be re-applied to sales already booked.

fee.title: Change booking fee
fee.desc: The booking fee percentage for this event only.
fee.invalid: Enter a percentage between 0 and 100 with up to two decimals.
fee.apply: Re-apply to sales already booked to this event
fee.applyHelp: Every booked sale (and its refunds) is re-posted at the new rate: the old postings are reversed, never edited. Do this before settling with the organiser.
fee.futureHelp: Only sales imported or matched from now on use the new rate; booked sales keep the rate they were calculated with.

scopes.allHelp: Every booked sale (and its refunds) is re-posted at the new rate; old postings are reversed, never edited. Use before settling.
scopes.fromHelp: Sales made on or after this date use the new rate; earlier sales keep theirs (e.g. 7 % until yesterday, 10 % from today).
scopes.futureHelp: Booked sales keep the rate they were calculated with.

fee.basis: How the booking fee is charged

bases.ADDED: Added on top of the ticket price
bases.GROSS: Included — % of what the customer paid
bases.NET: Included — % of paid amount after Stripe fee

basisHelp.ADDED: Customer pays ticket + fee. €35 ticket + 10 % = €38.50 paid → booking fee €3.50, organiser €35.00.
basisHelp.GROSS: Fee is a share of the amount paid. €38.50 paid at 10 % → fee €3.85.
basisHelp.NET: Fee is a share of the amount paid after Stripe's fee.

basisShort.NET: of amount paid after Stripe fee

pay.title: Pay organiser
pay.desc: Settlement for {organiser}. The payment is recorded as its own ledger entry.
pay.overpay: This pays {v} more than is due (overpaid).

payEdit.title: Edit payment
payEdit.desc: Changing the amount, date, method or reference reverses the original ledger entry and posts a corrected one.
payEdit.eventHint: Links the payment to an event and its organiser. Only {c} events are listed — the payment currency must match.
payEdit.noEvent: Not linked to an event (organiser account only)
payEdit.organiserChange: This moves the payment from {from} to {to}.

payDelete.title: Delete this payment?
payDelete.desc: Financial records never disappear: the payment is kept, marked VOIDED, and its ledger entry is reversed.

payments.title: Organiser payments
payments.desc: Every payment for this event, including edited and deleted (voided) ones.

tx.traceDesc: Each row is a Stripe transaction; open it to see the order, charge, fees and ledger postings.

exp.title: Expenses
exp.tabDesc: Platform costs for this event (venue, artist, marketing…). They reduce Bilit's profit and are never deducted from the organiser.
exp.desc: Recorded in the event currency and posted to the ledger.
exp.emptyDesc: Add venue, artist, marketing and other costs to see the event's true profit.
exp.name: Expense
exp.borneByHint: Who carries the cost. Organiser = deducted from their settlement.
exp.receiptHint: PDF, PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 10 MB
exp.receiptFailed: Saved, but the receipt upload failed
exp.deleteDesc: The expense is kept, marked as deleted, and its ledger entry is reversed.
exp.platformNote: Platform cost: reduces Bilit's profit on this event. It is not charged to or deducted from the organiser.

summary.title: Financial summary
summary.desc: Sales, booking fee, settlement and profit for this event.

sales.title: Sales report
sales.desc: Every order with refunds, Stripe fee and booking fee.

transactions.title: Stripe transactions
transactions.desc: All balance transactions booked to the event.

payments.title: Organiser payments
payments.desc: Payment history including edits and voids.

ledger.title: Ledger entries
ledger.desc: Double-entry postings tagged with this event.

statement.title: Organiser statement
statement.desc: Running balance of everything owed to and paid to the organiser.

eventReport.title: Event report
eventReport.desc: Sales, refunds, booking fee, processing fees, cashback, every payment against this event, and the organiser's balance across all events. Organiser copy.

eventReportInternal.title: Event report (internal)
eventReportInternal.desc: The same report with gross sales, booking fees and Bilit profit. For Bilit only.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.desc: Every financial change to this event, who made it and why.

events.title: Events — financials
events.sub: Every event with its sales, booking fee, organiser settlement and Bilit profit. Amounts are never mixed across currencies.

overview.title: Sales overview
overview.sub: All events: ticket sales, booking fees, organiser payments, expenses and Bilit profit.
overview.empty: No financial activity in this period
overview.emptyDesc: Choose a longer period or import Stripe transactions.
overview.outstandingHint: Due but not yet paid, as of the end of the period
overview.convertedNote: Indicative, at the rates in Finance settings. Never used for postings.
overview.missingRates: No rate set for {list}; those amounts are left out of the converted totals.
overview.none: No profit or loss booked in this period.

orgFin.title: Financial account
orgFin.expensesHint: Bilit's own costs on this organiser's events (not deducted from them)
orgFin.unassigned: Some payments are not tied to a specific event; they count towards the organiser's total but not to any single event.
orgFin.profitHint: Booking fees − Stripe fees and costs borne by Bilit

portalUsers.title: Organiser portal access
portalUsers.desc: Members who may see this organiser's own figures under “My finances”.
portalUsers.none: No one has portal access yet.
portalUsers.note: Portal users see only this organiser's live sales, booking fees, settlement and payments — never Bilit's profit, costs or other organisers. Invite the person under Members first (a Viewer role is enough).

portal.title: My finances
portal.sub: Sales, booking fees and payments for {name}.

fx.title: Reporting currency
fx.desc: Optional: show global totals converted into one currency.
fx.currencyHint: Leave empty to show each currency separately only
fx.note: Rates are indicative and used only for the converted overview. Every calculation and posting stays in the event's own currency.

fin.feeRecover: Booking fee to recover from organiser
fin.feeRecoverHint: Booking fee was refunded to customers. Under the platform policy the booking fee is non-refundable for Bilit, so this amount is charged to the organiser (already deducted from what they are due).

policy.title: Refund policy
policy.desc: How refunds affect Bilit's booking fee.
policy.nonRefundableHelp: Refunds never reduce Bilit's booking fee. If a booking fee is refunded to a customer, the organiser is charged for it (shown as “booking fee to recover from organiser”).
policy.note: Changing this re-calculates all existing refunds (old postings are reversed, never edited).

impact.title: Effect on Bilit's cash (preview)
impact.own: Bilit's own money after everything owed
impact.notEnough: Not enough {c} available right now — part of the balance is still pending in Stripe, or move money in from another currency.
impact.note: Nothing is paid or recorded until you press the button. Paying what is owed does not change Bilit's own money; only an overpayment does.

overview.title: Bookkeeping
overview.sub: Company books: income, costs, supplier invoices, VAT and payroll — every figure comes from the ledger.
overview.emptyDesc: Upload a supplier invoice or add an expense to get started.
overview.plDesc: All income and costs booked in {c} for the period.

doc.title: Invoices & expenses
doc.sub: Supplier invoices (to pay) and expenses (already paid). Upload the PDF or photo; every document is posted to the ledger.
doc.billDesc: A supplier invoice Bilit owes until it is paid.
doc.expenseDesc: A cost that has already been paid (card, bank, cash or by an employee).
doc.search: Search supplier, invoice no. or description
doc.eventHint: Optional — the cost then counts towards that event's profit
doc.fileHint: PDF, PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 15 MB
doc.fileFailed: Saved, but the file upload failed
doc.emptyDesc: Upload supplier invoices and add expenses; they are booked to the right cost account automatically.
doc.deleteDesc: The document is kept, marked as deleted, and its ledger entries are reversed.
doc.dupTitle: This looks like a document that is already in the books
doc.dupConfirm: This is a different document — save it anyway

emp.title: Employees
emp.sub: Staff on the payroll. Each employee has their own country and currency.
emp.desc: Personal and payroll details. Bank details are encrypted.
emp.forbidden: You need the payroll permission to see employees.
emp.emptyDesc: Add your staff to create payslips for them.
emp.name: Name

ps.title: Payslips
ps.sub: Enter pay and deductions from your accountant or payroll provider; the system works out net pay, year-to-date totals and issues the PDF.
ps.forbidden: You need the payroll permission to see payslips.
ps.desc: Amounts are entered by hand — nothing is calculated from tax tables.
ps.label: Description
ps.notesHint: Printed at the bottom of the PDF
ps.tooMuch: Deductions are larger than gross pay.
ps.manualNote: Check figures against your payroll provider. Issued payslips cannot be changed — void and reissue instead.
ps.noEmployeesDesc: Payslips are created for employees listed under Employees.
ps.emptyDesc: Create a payslip, check it as a draft PDF, then issue it.
ps.finaliseDesc: It gets a number, is booked to the ledger and the PDF is stored. It can no longer be edited.
ps.voidDesc: The payslip is kept, marked void, and its ledger entries are reversed. Issue a corrected payslip afterwards.

pay.title: Stripe payment
pay.desc: Everything Stripe reports about this payment: status, decline reason, risk check, card, refunds and disputes.

issue.disputedBody: The customer disputed this payment with their bank. Respond in the Stripe dashboard before the deadline.
issue.risk: Stripe flagged this payment as risky

refund.title: Refund payment
refund.desc: Refund {customer} through Stripe. The money goes back to the card used.
refund.ticketOnlySub: Platform policy: the booking fee ({fee}) is non-refundable and stays with Bilit.
refund.fullSub: The booking fee is refunded too — it is charged back to the organiser.
refund.customSub: Partial refund of a chosen amount.
refund.keepFee: Bilit keeps its booking fee (organiser bears the refund)
refund.noteHint: Kept with the refund and in the audit log
refund.confirmBody: {amount} will be refunded to the customer's card through Stripe. This cannot be undone.

list.title: Payments
list.sub: Every card payment in Stripe — including declined and pending ones that never reach the books — with the reason and risk.
list.search: Search customer, email, order or charge id
list.emptyDesc: Run a Stripe sync to import payments, including failed ones.

inv.title: Invoices & credit notes
inv.desc: Issue an invoice for the sale (or a VAT invoice with the customer's business details) and a credit note for each refund. Documents are numbered, stored and never changed.
inv.voidDesc: It stays on file marked void; you can then issue a corrected one with a new number.
inv.vatDesc: For a business customer: their (company) name and address are required; add their VAT number if they have one.
inv.plainDesc: A receipt-style invoice for the customer, from the Stripe payment details.
inv.immutable: Once issued the document cannot be edited — void it and issue a new one if something is wrong.
inv.listSub: Invoices, VAT invoices and credit notes issued to ticket buyers.
inv.listEmptyDesc: Issue them from a transaction (Transactions → open a sale).

invSettings.title: Invoices
invSettings.desc: Seller details and VAT treatment printed on customer invoices, VAT invoices and credit notes.
invSettings.feeVat: VAT rate on the booking fee (%)
invSettings.feeVatHint: Booking fees are charged VAT-inclusive at this rate

modes.AGENT: Sold as agent for the organiser (no Bilit VAT)

ticketModeHint.AGENT: The ticket price belongs to the organiser; the invoice says so.
ticketModeHint.INCLUDED: Use if Bilit itself sells the tickets.

invSettings.accountantNote: Confirm the VAT treatment with your accountant before issuing VAT invoices.
invSettings.registeredInHint: Used in contracts: "a company registered in …"

acc.title: Accountant pack & AI review
acc.desc: Everything your accountant needs for a period — PDF report plus CSVs (ledger, P&L, VAT, events & settlement, organiser payments, expenses, payroll, refunds, payouts, invoices) — and automatic checks for gaps.
acc.aiDisabled: Set up the AI accountant under Finance settings first
acc.packNote: The pack includes the latest AI review for the same period, if there is one. Exports need a recent sign-in.
acc.noIssues: No gaps found by the automatic checks.
acc.aiSetup: Add an OpenAI API key under Finance settings → AI accountant to have the books reviewed by an AI bookkeeper.
acc.aiDisclaimer: AI suggestions are a second pair of eyes, not professional advice — confirm anything important with your accountant.

ai.title: AI accountant (OpenAI)
ai.desc: An AI bookkeeper reviews each period for gaps, inconsistencies and things your accountant will ask about.
ai.enableHelp: Runs only when someone presses “Run AI accountant review” on the Reports page.
ai.keyHint: From platform.openai.com → API keys. Stored encrypted, never shown again.
ai.keySet: Key saved ({hint}). Enter a new one to replace it.
ai.modelHint: Any OpenAI chat model your key can use, e.g. gpt-4.1 or gpt-4o
ai.instructionsHint: Added to the review prompt (e.g. your VAT scheme, year end, things to focus on)
ai.instructionsPh: e.g. We are UK VAT registered on the standard scheme; year end 31 March. Pay particular attention to organiser balances.
ai.privacy: Only aggregated figures are sent to OpenAI (totals, events, categories, checks). Customer names, emails and card details are never sent; employees are referred to by employee number only.
ai.voiceEnable: Enable voice questions and spoken answers
ai.voiceEnableHelp: Uses the same OpenAI key (it needs access to audio models). Recordings are sent once for transcription and never stored.
ai.autoSpeak: Read answers aloud automatically by default
ai.speedHint: 1 = normal, 1.25 = a bit faster, 0.9 = slower. Each user can change it in the widget.

refunds.title: Refunds
refunds.sub: Every refund and chargeback, the event it belongs to, and how much of it was ticket price or booking fee. Refunds follow their sale: link the sale to an event and its refunds link too.
refunds.feeRecover: Booking fee to recover from organisers
refunds.unlinkedDesc: These refunds belong to sales whose event is not set up yet. Create the events (choose the organiser and booking fee) and the sales and refunds link automatically — or link single refunds by hand below.
refunds.eventExistsHint: The event exists — link the sales/refunds by hand below.
refunds.noEventHint: No event with this code yet — create it.
refunds.search: Search customer, email, order or event code
refunds.help: Linking a refund whose sale is not linked links the sale too (the refund follows its sale). Under the platform policy the booking fee is non-refundable: if a refund includes it, the organiser is charged for it.

recover.title: Booking fees to recover from organisers
recover.desc: Booking fees refunded to customers (e.g. cancelled events). Under the platform policy the organiser pays them back: the amount is deducted from what you owe them, and if their balance goes negative they owe Bilit the difference.

aichat.title: Ask the AI accountant
aichat.pageSub: Ask questions about payments, profits, refunds and organiser settlements, and run a full AI review of the books.
aichat.chatDesc: Answers come from the live ledger figures (no customer personal data is sent).
aichat.intro: I'm your finance assistant. I can look up anything in the books, Wise and Stripe, and prepare changes (record, mark paid, correct or void a payment) — you confirm each one before it happens.
aichat.s1: Check all payments to Pegasus this year against Wise and Stripe
aichat.s2: Which organisers are still owed money?
aichat.s3: Are there Wise transfers that are not in the books?
aichat.s4: Run the bookkeeping checks and tell me what to fix
aichat.s6: How much profit did we make this month?
aichat.disclaimer: Answers come from your live books via OpenAI. Changes only happen when you press Confirm.
aichat.setup: Add an OpenAI API key and enable the AI accountant in Finance settings to ask questions here.
aichat.noPermission: Needs finance manager rights to confirm.

payagent.title: AI payment agent
payagent.desc: Paste a bank / Wise / Stripe confirmation or type an instruction (e.g. “Paid Demian €8,000 by Wise yesterday, ref 2372969752”). The AI bookkeeper reads it, matches the organiser, checks the balance and duplicates, and proposes the payment. Nothing is posted until you confirm.
payagent.textHint: One or several payments. Include who, how much, currency, date and the transfer reference if you have them.
payagent.placeholder:
e.g. Sent €2,500 to Pegasus Events for the Vienna show via Wise on 3 Oct, transfer #2401188234

or paste the Wise / bank confirmation here…
payagent.privacy: The text and the organiser balances are sent to OpenAI; ticket buyers' details are not
payagent.notReady: The AI accountant is not set up. Add an OpenAI key under Finance settings → AI accountant.
payagent.question: Question:
payagent.none: No payment to an organiser was found in the text.
payagent.dupOk: I confirm this is a separate transfer, not a duplicate
payagent.record: {n, plural, =0 {Record payments} one {Record # payment} other {Record # payments}}
payagent.recorded: {n, plural, one {# payment recorded} other {# payments recorded}}

wise.title: Wise bank feed
wise.sub: Read-only connection to Bilit's Wise account. Transfers you send from Wise are imported, matched to organiser payments, and anything not yet in the books is flagged so you can record it with one click.
wise.connectDesc: Uses a read-only Wise API token. Bilit can see balances and transactions but can never send money or change anything in Wise.
wise.step1: In Wise Business, open Settings → Developer tools → API tokens (wise.com/settings/api-tokens).
wise.step2: Create a new token with “Read only” access for the business profile and copy it.
wise.step3: Paste it below. Transfers, incoming payouts, card spend and fees are imported straight away.
wise.tokenHint: Stored encrypted; only the last characters are ever shown again.
wise.adminOnly: Only finance admins can connect a bank account.
wise.readOnlyNote: Wise is real money, so everything imported here belongs to the LIVE books. Ticket buyers' data is never involved.
wise.connInfo: Token {hint} · last synced {when} · syncs automatically every 30 minutes
wise.disconnectDesc: The token and keys are deleted. Already imported transactions and recorded payments stay. You can reconnect any time.
wise.toRecordTitle: {n, plural, one {# Wise transfer is not in the books} other {# Wise transfers are not in the books}}
wise.toRecordDesc: Book each one as an organiser payment, an expense or a supplier invoice — or mark it as something else (own account, loan, salary…).
wise.scaDesc: Transfers, incoming Stripe payouts, card spend and fees already come in through the Wise activity feed. Statements add running balances; for those, Wise requires strong customer authentication: download the public key file (.pem) and upload it in Wise → Settings → Developer tools → API tokens → Manage public keys, then press Sync now.
wise.copyFailed: Could not copy — select the key and copy it manually
wise.scaOk: Statements are connected: incoming money (e.g. Stripe payouts), conversions and fees are imported too.
wise.emptyToRecord: Every Wise transfer is in the books
wise.emptyDesc: Press Sync now to import the latest activity from Wise.
wise.ignoreDesc: The transfer stays imported but is no longer flagged as missing from the books.
wise.ignorePlaceholder: e.g. own account transfer, supplier invoice, salary
wise.liveNote: Payments recorded from Wise are posted to the LIVE books with the Wise transfer number as reference, so they are matched automatically.
wise.aiIntro: These are transfers Bilit sent from its Wise account that are not yet recorded in the books. For each one decide, as Bilit's accountant, whether it is a payment to an organiser (match the organiser by recipient name), and propose it with the given Wise bank reference. Transfers that are clearly not organiser payments (own accounts, suppliers, salaries, tax) must NOT be proposed — list them in warnings with what they probably are.
wise.expenseHint: Book as a paid expense (no supplier invoice to track)
wise.invoiceHint: Book as a supplier invoice, already paid from Wise — attach the PDF
wise.bulkNote: One record is created per transaction, dated on the Wise date, in its own currency, with “Wise #number” as reference so it stays linked. VAT is not split — edit an item afterwards if the supplier charged VAT.

expense.title: Book {n} as expenses
expense.desc: Each becomes a paid expense in the chosen category, payee = Wise recipient.

bill.title: Book {n} as supplier invoices
bill.desc: Each becomes a supplier invoice marked paid from Wise; attach the PDFs later under Bookkeeping → Invoices.

organiser.title: Record {n} organiser payments
organiser.desc: Each becomes a payment to the chosen organiser (whole organiser, not split by event).

ignore.title: Mark {n} as not organiser payments
ignore.desc: They stay imported but are no longer flagged as missing from the books.

partner.title: Record {n} payments to a partner
partner.desc: Each becomes a profit-share payment to the chosen partner (e.g. the developer).

wise.settingsNotConnected: Not connected. Connect it on the Wise page.

pshare.title: Profit share
pshare.sub: Partners who earn a percentage of each event's profit.
pshare.subPartner: {name} earns {pct}% of each event's profit. The share is booked automatically as a cost and kept up to date as sales and refunds come in.
pshare.noPartnersDesc: Add someone who earns a percentage of each event's profit, e.g. the web developer.
pshare.inactive: This partner is inactive: shares already earned stay owed, but no new shares are booked.
pshare.overpaid: Paid more than earned so far
pshare.noPaymentsDesc: Record payments to the partner as you make them, or book them from the Wise page.
pshare.voidDesc: The payment is kept, marked VOIDED, and its ledger entry is reversed; the amount becomes owed again.
pshare.howItWorks: How it works: for every event the share is {pct}% of Bilit's profit on that event (booking fees and other income less Stripe fees and Bilit's own event costs), before profit shares. It is booked as an expense (6950 Profit Share) owed to the partner (2400 Profit Share Payable). When an event's profit changes, the difference is booked automatically. Events are grouped by the month they take place.
pshare.partnerDesc: The percentage applies to Bilit's profit on each event.
pshare.name: Name
pshare.lossesCount: Losses reduce the share (otherwise an event with a loss gives 0)
pshare.changeNote: Changing the % or rules re-calculates every event; the differences are booked as adjustments.
pshare.paymentDesc: Money Bilit paid the partner. It reduces what is owed in that currency.
pshare.currencyHint: Currency of the share you are paying off
pshare.referenceHint: For Wise use “Wise #<number>” so it links to the Wise transfer

position.title: Financial Overview
position.sub: What Bilit holds, what it owes, what it is owed and what is left — from live Stripe and Wise balances and the ledger.
position.periodNote: Cash, debts and settlements are current balances; revenue, profit and cash flow follow the selected period.
position.pickCurrency: Pick a currency to see the summary cards (no exchange rates are available to combine currencies).
position.fxNote: Combined figures are converted to {c} at {source} ({rates}) and are indicative only — each currency is paid separately.
position.showRecords: Show the records behind this figure

cards.netProfitHint: After Stripe fees, refunds, running costs and profit share
cards.inventoryHint: No stock is held — tickets are sold as agent
cards.shortHint: Extra money needed to pay everything owed in this currency
cards.noShortfallHint: Every amount owed can be paid from cash held in its currency

summary.title: Financial summary
summary.sub: Current position per currency. Click an underlined amount to see its records.
summary.formula: Left after paying all = verified cash (Stripe available + pending, Wise) − amounts owed to organisers − other unpaid liabilities. Money owed to us, money in transit and the unreadable Stripe wallet are never counted as cash.

cash.title: Cash and bank
cash.sub: Read live from Stripe and from the latest Wise sync.

liab.title: Debts and money owed to us
liab.sub: Each debt is counted once, from its own source.
liab.receivable: Owed to Bilit — not counted as cash

org.title: Organiser settlements
org.sub: Per organiser and currency, all time. Click a row for payments and records.
org.owing: Events where the organiser owes Bilit (already netted): {list}
org.note: Total due = organiser share − Stripe fees recharged − deductions (fees, organiser expenses, adjustments), from each event's agreement. Payments made for the organiser as a whole are applied to the oldest events first to work out what is due now; events still to come are due later.

flow.title: Cash flow
flow.sub: Money in and out of each account in the period, from the books. Moves between Bilit's own accounts are not counted as income or spending.
flow.note: Stripe is reconciled to the Stripe API to the cent. The bank side is only as complete as the bookkeeping: Wise transfers that are not booked yet make it differ from the real Wise balance.

profit.title: Profit
profit.sub: For the selected period, from the ledger.
profit.note: Revenue = booking fees and other Bilit income (ticket money that belongs to organisers is excluded). Direct costs = Stripe fees, refunds and chargebacks borne by Bilit, event costs. Running costs include partner profit share.

drill.sub: The ledger lines behind this figure.
drill.capped: Showing the latest 1,000 lines only — narrow the period to see older ones.
drill.note: Reversed lines are corrections and cancel out with their reversal entry.

fx.title: Exchange rates to {c}
fx.sub: Source: {source} · {at}. Indicative only — each currency is paid in its own currency.
fx.connectXe: Using Wise / manual rates. Connect XE to use XE mid-market rates:

aiacc.title: Bilit AI Accountant
aiacc.setup: An admin needs to add an OpenAI API key and enable the AI accountant under Finance settings → AI accountant. Voice can be switched on there too.
aiacc.intro: Ask me about profit, revenue, Stripe fees, organiser settlements, cash or reconciliation. I only use figures calculated by the finance system, show how each one was calculated, and cannot change anything. You can also speak or ask in Persian.
aiacc.introFa: درباره‌ی سود، فروش، کارمزد استرایپ، تسویه با برگزارکنندگان، نقدینگی یا تطبیق حساب‌ها بپرسید. فقط از ارقامی استفاده می‌کنم که سیستم مالی محاسبه کرده، روش محاسبه را نشان می‌دهم و چیزی را تغییر نمی‌دهم. می‌توانید صحبت کنید یا انگلیسی بپرسید.

ask.profit: Analyse our overall profitability to date: revenue, Stripe fees, refunds, expenses and net profit, per currency.
ask.balance: Explain the current cash balance and what would remain if we paid all current liabilities.
ask.events: Show revenue, costs, profit and organiser settlement for each event, and which event was the most profitable.
ask.fees: How much have we paid in Stripe fees, how much was recharged to organisers, and what share of gross sales is that?
ask.settlements: How much do we currently owe each organiser, how much has been paid, and what is due now?
ask.expenses: Are there any unusual or unusually high expenses recently? Show the largest costs.
ask.recon: Which Stripe transactions have not been reconciled, and what figures does that affect?
ask.compare: Compare this month's revenue and profit with last month.

sugFa.compare: این ماه در برابر ماه قبل

askFa.profit: سود واقعی بیلیت تا امروز چقدر بوده؟ درآمد، کارمزد استرایپ، استردادها، هزینه‌ها و سود خالص را به تفکیک ارز بگو.
askFa.balance: موجودی نقد فعلی را توضیح بده؛ اگر تمام تعهدات فعلی را پرداخت کنیم، وضعیت نقدینگی چطور می‌شود؟
askFa.events: برای هر ایونت، درآمد، هزینه، سود و تسویه‌ی برگزارکننده را جداگانه نشان بده. کدام ایونت بیشترین سود را داشته؟
askFa.fees: چقدر کارمزد به استرایپ پرداخت کردیم، چقدرش به برگزارکننده‌ها شارژ شد و چند درصد فروش ناخالص است؟
askFa.settlements: چقدر به برگزارکننده‌ها بدهکاریم؟ چقدر پرداخت شده و چقدر باقی مانده و الان سررسید است؟
askFa.expenses: آیا اخیراً هزینه‌ی غیرعادی یا خیلی زیاد داشته‌ایم؟ بزرگ‌ترین هزینه‌ها را نشان بده.
askFa.recon: کدام تراکنش‌ها هنوز با حسابداری تطبیق داده نشده‌اند و روی کدام ارقام اثر دارند؟
askFa.compare: فروش و سود این ماه را با ماه قبل مقایسه کن.

aiacc.askAbout: Explain the figure "{label}" ({value}) for the period I'm viewing: what it includes, how it is calculated, and whether it is final.
aiacc.askAboutFa: رقم «{label}» ({value}) را برای همین دوره توضیح بده: شامل چه چیزهایی است، چطور محاسبه شده و آیا قطعی است؟
aiacc.freshness: Data freshness — Stripe last synced: {stripe}; Wise last synced: {wise}
aiacc.recording: Recording… {s}s — press stop when you have finished
aiacc.heard: Recognised — check or correct the text, then press send.
aiacc.micUnsupported: This browser cannot record audio. Type your question instead.
aiacc.micDenied: Microphone access was blocked. Allow the microphone for this site and try again.
aiacc.tooShort: That recording was too short. Hold on a little longer.
aiacc.voiceFailed: The answer could not be read aloud.
aiacc.voiceOff: Voice is not switched on (Finance settings → AI accountant → Voice)
aiacc.placeholder: Ask about profit, fees, settlements, cash…
aiacc.placeholderFa: درباره‌ی سود، کارمزد، تسویه یا نقدینگی بپرسید…
aiacc.rateLimited: Too many questions in a short time. Please wait a few minutes and try again.
aiacc.disclaimer: Read-only. Figures come from the finance system's own calculations; the question and data summaries go to OpenAI. Questions are logged in the audit trail; recordings are not stored.

xe.title: XE exchange rates
xe.desc: Live XE mid-market rates for the converted £ totals on the Financial Overview and in the AI Accountant. Needs an XE Currency Data API account (xe.com/xecurrencydata).
xe.keyHint: From your XE Currency Data account. Stored encrypted, never shown again.
xe.keySet: Key saved ({hint}). Enter a new one to replace it.
xe.note: Used only for converted (indicative) totals; nothing is posted at these rates. Rates are refreshed at most every 15 minutes. Without XE, Wise's live rate is used.

forecast.title: Cash forecast
forecast.sub: Estimated cash in the next days, from what is already in the books: Stripe money still pending (by release date), what organisers are owed (by event date), unpaid supplier invoices (by due date), wages and profit share owed, and optional running costs.
forecast.failed: The forecast could not be loaded.
forecast.totalIn: Free cash in {days} days, all currencies in {c}
forecast.short: {c} runs short on {date} unless money is moved in from another currency or payments are delayed.
forecast.assumptions: Estimate, not a promise. Organisers are assumed paid {payDays} day(s) after their event.
forecast.runRateOn: Running costs = average of the last 3 full months.
forecast.excluded: Not included: future ticket sales, new refunds, currency conversions and invoices not yet entered.

monitor.title: Checks & forecast
monitor.desc: Thresholds for the automatic checks on the Financial Overview (refund rate, Stripe fees, margins, duplicate invoices, webhooks) and assumptions for the cash forecast.
monitor.note: Checks only raise alerts; they never change records. Events with fewer orders than the minimum are not checked.

f.organiserPayDays: Pay organisers N days after event
f.forecastRunRate: Include estimated running costs in the forecast

h.feePctOverMedian: Percentage points above the median of same-currency events. Default {d}
h.expenseSpikeX: This month vs recent average. Default {d}
h.duplicateBillDays: Same supplier + amount within N days. Default {d}

payouts.title: Send money
payouts.sub: Pay organisers, profit-share partners and supplier invoices straight from Bilit's Stripe financial account. Each payment is booked automatically.
payouts.notSetUp: Stripe payouts are not set up ({mode})
payouts.notSetUpDesc: Add a restricted Stripe key with Global Payouts permissions and choose the financial account to pay from.
payouts.noBalance: The financial account has no balance yet.
payouts.historyDesc: Newest first. Status comes from Stripe; failed or returned payments are un-booked automatically.
payouts.cancelDesc: Stripe will try to stop {amount} to {name}. Only possible while it is still processing.
payouts.sendDesc: Choose who to pay. Nothing is sent until you review and confirm.
payouts.reviewDesc: Check the details. Sending asks you to confirm your identity.
payouts.sent: Payment sent to Stripe and booked
payouts.sentFailed: Stripe reports the payment failed — nothing was booked
payouts.recipientHint: Recipients are created in the Stripe Dashboard.
payouts.noMethods: This recipient has no payout method yet — add one in Stripe.
payouts.toCurrencyHint: Leave empty for the same currency. Another currency is converted by Stripe at the quoted rate.
payouts.descriptionHint: Shown in Stripe and on Bilit's records.
payouts.overpay: Pay more than owed (I know this is more than the balance)
payouts.allowDuplicate: This is a separate payment, send it anyway
payouts.copMismatch: Bank name check: not a full match
payouts.ackMismatch: I have checked the account details with the payee and want to send anyway
payouts.bookNote: When Stripe accepts the payment it is recorded as a payment (method Stripe, reference = Stripe payment id). If Stripe later reports it failed or returned, that record is voided automatically.
payouts.recipientsAtStripe: Add or edit recipients and their bank details in Stripe → Payouts → Recipients.
payouts.how: Money leaves the Stripe financial account through Stripe Global Payouts. Only finance admins can send, and every payment needs a fresh identity check. Organiser balances, partner shares and unpaid invoices are checked before sending, duplicates within 3 days are blocked unless confirmed, and Stripe's status is re-checked every 30 minutes.

settings.title: Stripe payouts — {mode}
settings.desc: The key and account used by Send money. Separate from the read-only key that imports Stripe data.
settings.keyHint: Stripe Dashboard → Developers → API keys → Create restricted key. Stored encrypted, never shown again.
settings.keySet: Key saved ({hint}). Paste a new one to replace it.
settings.accountHint: Loaded from Stripe when the key is saved.
settings.permsTitle: The restricted key needs (Stripe refuses full sk_live keys for payouts):
settings.note: Global Payouts must be enabled on the Stripe account. Switch the TEST/LIVE toggle to set up the other mode.

cc.title: Finance overview
cc.sub: Ticket revenue, fees, organiser settlements and Bilit's profit — straight from the ledger and imported Stripe data. Each currency is shown separately; nothing is converted.
cc.comparing: Percentages compare with the previous equivalent period ({from} – {to}).
cc.noCompare: Choose a bounded period (e.g. This month) to compare with the previous period.

d.gross: Everything customers paid for tickets in the period, before refunds and fees.
d.fees: All Stripe fees on these transactions, including the part recharged to organisers.
d.refunds: Money returned to customers, plus lost disputes.
d.net: Gross − refunds & chargebacks − Stripe fees: the money actually kept from sales. Not profit.
d.liabilities: Organisers' share of the period's sales (after commission, refunds and the fees they bear).
d.paid: Settlement payments made to organisers in the period.
d.outstanding: Still owed to organisers at the end of the period, across all time (not limited to this period).
d.profit: Bilit's revenue minus Bilit's own costs, from the ledger P&L. Organisers' money is never counted.

cc.askAi: Ask the AI accountant about these figures
cc.chartDesc: Gross sales, net collected, refunds and Stripe fees from the ledger. Hover for exact values; click a series to hide it.
cc.noData: No transactions in this period and currency.
cc.alertsDesc: Counted from imported data; each item opens the place to resolve it.

al.notConnected: Stripe is not connected in this mode
al.unmatched: {n} transaction(s) without a matching event code
al.refunds: {n} refund(s) not linked to an event
al.payoutsFailed: {n} Stripe payout(s) failed or returned (30 days)
al.owed: {n} organiser(s) with a balance awaiting settlement

cc.breakdownDesc: Three separate statements for the selected period. They are not added to each other, so no fee or refund is counted twice.

bd.barLabel: Share of gross sales: net collected, refunds, Stripe fees
bd.netHint: Includes money that belongs to organisers.
bd.feesBilitHint: Fees recharged to organisers ({v}) are excluded.
bd.otherCostsHint: Expenses, profit share, bank charges etc. posted in the period.
bd.orgEarnedHint: Their share of the period's sales.
bd.orgOutstandingHint: Balance owed at the end of the period — includes earlier periods.

cc.recentDesc: Latest Stripe activity in this currency.
cc.noTx: No transactions yet in this currency.

plinks.title: Payment links
plinks.sub: Create a branded payment page for an event and price, share the link, and each payment flows into the books like any other Stripe sale.
plinks.refreshed: Checked {n} open checkout(s) with Stripe — {paid} paid
plinks.keyWarn: Links will try the Stripe import key ({hint}) in {mode} mode. If that key is read-only, buyers will see “not set up yet” — add a restricted key with Checkout Sessions write access.
plinks.listDesc: Newest first. Click the sold figure to see each buyer.
plinks.emptyDesc: Pick an event, set the price and your branding, then share the link.
plinks.how: The link opens a page with your logo, colours, the event name and the price. Paying opens Stripe Checkout with the same branding. The sale carries the event code, so the Stripe import matches it to the event and books the booking fee automatically.
plinks.dialogDesc: {mode} mode. The link is copied to your clipboard when it is created.
plinks.pickEventHint: Fills in the name, code, currency and booking fee, and makes sales match this event.
plinks.eventCodeHint: Used to match sales to an event.
plinks.locked: This link already has payments, so price, fee and currency are locked. Create a new link for a new price.
plinks.displayNameHint: Defaults to your organisation's branding name.
plinks.stripeOnly: Applies on the Stripe checkout page.
plinks.imageHint: Shown next to the item on Stripe checkout.
plinks.previewNote: Your logo from Settings → Branding is shown on the page and on Stripe checkout.
plinks.created: Payment link created — copied to clipboard
plinks.keyDesc: Stored encrypted and never shown again. Use a restricted key with Checkout Sessions read + write.
plinks.keyNone: No dedicated key — the import key ({hint}) is used.
plinks.keyHint: Stripe Dashboard → Developers → API keys → Create restricted key → Checkout Sessions: Write.
plinks.sessionsDesc: Every checkout opened from this link. Open ones expire at Stripe after 24 hours.
plinks.noSessions: No one has opened checkout yet.

pub.unavailable: This payment link is no longer available.
pub.receipt: A receipt has been sent to {email}.
pub.pending: Your payment is still being confirmed. You can close this page; you'll get an email from Stripe.
